as_read: Abstracts conflict on lipid markers, and no trial reaches rule 2 for plain theobromine at label amounts: the abstracts name no primary outcome for theobromine alone, or test it with cocoa, or don't state the dose.

quote.text: These findings do not suggest that theobromine alone contributes to the proposed cardioprotective effects of cocoa.

proposed_decision_text: The labels print plain theobromine at 250 mg or 400 mg per serving and carry no heart or cholesterol purpose. This is an abstracts-only review, and no study read meets the rule for credit. The stored trial gave 850 mg pure theobromine in a daily drink to 152 healthy adults for 4 weeks and raised HDL cholesterol by 0.16 mmol/L, but the abstract names no primary outcome and the amount is more than twice any label (PMID 23595874). A crossover of 44 adults with low HDL cholesterol found 500 mg/day was not effective on HDL cholesterol (PMID 28971099), and the same size and design of study reported no fasting HDL change, lower LDL cholesterol and unfavorable postprandial glucose and insulin responses (PMID 28645636), no improvement in endothelial function (PMID 29330660) and no change in cholesterol efflux (PMID 29797695); none of these abstracts names a primary outcome. A trial of 450 mg/day in 80 adults with metabolic syndrome improved waist and lipid ratios, but alongside a low-calorie diet and with no primary outcome named (PMID 37615657; related report PMID 40672541). The persistent cough trial of BC1036 named a primary outcome and it did not reach significance, but the abstract gives no dose (PMID 28839984). The blood pressure trial named a primary outcome, but tested theobromine in cocoa rather than alone (PMID 20823377).
clinician_items: 23420115: within-subjects study of 80 healthy participants; limited subjective effects at 250 mg, negative mood effects at higher doses (500 and 1000 mg tested), dose-dependent heart rate increase.
20823377: theobromine-enriched cocoa (979 mg) raised 24-hour ambulatory systolic pressure by 3.2 mmHg versus placebo (P<0.01) in 42 adults; central systolic was lower at 2 hours.
28645636: 500 mg/day raised hsCRP (1.2 mg/L, P = 0.017) and postprandial glucose, insulin and FFA in 44 adults.
stored_rating_note: positive_weak rests on 23595874 alone. Later 500 mg/day crossover reports (28971099, 28645636) did not find the HDL effect, though LDL fell. Erratum 39115149 exists for 37615657; its content isn't in PubMed's abstract field, so what it corrects is unread.
unread_notes: Abstracts only; no full text opened. Not opened: 15548587 (cough, title only), 28438412 (acute intake, title only), 29658370 (pregnant women, high-flavanol chocolate, title only), 15772863, 7862879. BC1036's dose may be in the full text of 28839984; it was not read, and the trial was null on its primary outcome per its abstract.
